so_the_finding_is_instrument_sensitive_a.a_race_the_instrument_hides: the streaming engine materialises weights per block; a pre-hook that reads module.weight forces a device synchronisation before the GEMM.  If the vendor path can start a GEMM against a partially-copied weight, a pre-hook masks exactly that -- so the NaN would be real in normal operation and invisible whenever anything synchronises.
so_the_finding_is_instrument_sensitive_a.or_the_instrument_causes_it: about 1,800 post-only hooks, each running a reduction on a fresh output tensor, is itself a perturbation, and it is the only configuration in which NaN appeared.

the_control_that_complicates_it.and_a_separate_six_tap_run: a narrower probe with pre-hooks on six named experts also found no NaN in any weight, scale, input or output -- including L02.ffn.experts.303.w1, which two earlier runs had reported NaN
the_control_that_complicates_it.probe: every expert linear in the first six blocks watched with BOTH a pre-hook and a post-hook -- 6,930 modules, 13,860 hooks -- counting isnan on the weight, the scale and the input before each call and on the output after it

CORRECTION.what_I_claimed: that the shipped oracle computes NaN inside routed-expert w1 GEMMs, measured in two single-forward processes and confirmed in a third by counting isnan directly (5 NaN taps of about 1,800)
CORRECTION.what_I_should_have_done: run the pre-hook control in the same session as the first NaN reading rather than publishing the mechanism from post-only hooks.  Three of my readings this session have been corrected by controls I ran afterwards; the controls are cheap and the corrections are not.

what_is_unaffected_either_way.the_device_is_deterministic: 305 from two different stores at two different context lengths
what_is_unaffected_either_way.the_intermediates_are_not_a_usable_compa: three separate single-forward processes produced three different summaries for the SAME post-norm row -- argmax 529, 4521 and 529, with min and max moving by up to 0.08.  That stands independently of the NaN question, and it is the fact that invalidates the depth bisection.
what_is_unaffected_either_way.the_token_is_stable: 13806 on every run of every probe, including the ones that reported NaN, and the committed four-token gold reproduces.  Grading the cells on TOKENS remains sound; grading them on intermediates does not.

answer: NaN was measured in three post-only-hook runs and NOT reproduced with pre-hooks attached, so the mechanism is unsettled -- see CORRECTION.  What is settled is that the oracle's INTERMEDIATES are not reproducible while its TOKEN is.

measured.method: a float64 sum-of-squares and a max captured per submodule output for the first six blocks, ONE forward per process, two separate processes

not_a_claim: the NaN's cause inside the vendor FP8 GEMM is not established
this says nothing about whether the accelerator is right
question: the shipped V4.1 oracle disagrees with itself run to run.  Where does the variation enter?
the_remedy_that_already_exists: tools/bisect_deepseek_v41_oracle_divergence.py carries an ``--expert-numeric-path fp4_dequantised`` path whose own comment says it 'keeps the declared numerics -- same FP4 codes, same E8M0 block scales, same activation quantisation -- and replaces only the vendor kernel that is broken on this GPU'.  That is exactly this situation, and testing it for NaN is the next step.

what_it_means_for_the_v41_verification.so_the_device_disagreeing_is_not_the_dev: 305 against 13806 cannot be read as a device defect while the comparator computes NaN in its expert path.  That does not make the device right; it makes the comparison unsafe in the direction I had been reading it.
what_it_means_for_the_v41_verification.the_intermediates_are_unusable: every cosine in the depth bisection was computed against a reference that contains NaN somewhere upstream, which is why its cosines are low everywhere and why three probes of the same row disagreed
what_it_means_for_the_v41_verification.the_token_is_stable_but_not_for_a_good_r: the oracle emits 13806 on every run and its final norm carries no NaN, so the NaN is masked somewhere between the expert and the residual.  A gold token that survives a NaN by masking is not a gold token anyone should grade against without saying so.

why_the_earlier_two_forward_probe_was_in: I first compared two forwards inside ONE process and read the differences as non-determinism.  That comparison is void on its own terms: the streaming engine materialises and releases weights per block and is not re-entrant, so a second forward is not a repeat.  The result survives only because ONE forward per process still shows NaN -- which is what makes the runs differ.
